problem.title: Automatic activation identity rejected by retained runtime evidence volume
problem.user_impact: A large retained .coding-tools evidence tree could block automatic activation before source identity was evaluated.

reproduction.pre_fix_behavior: workspaceIdentity rejected the current repository before filtering retained runtime evidence.

patch.summary: gitStatus now applies rooted .coding-tools exclude pathspecs before the bounded output and source-entry checks; actual source-entry limits remain enforced.
patch.pathspec_policy: :(top)** plus rooted .coding-tools exclusions; Windows uses case-insensitive exclusion.

validation.focused_regression: 2,001 retained evidence files are ignored; evidence edits do not change the source fingerprint; source edits do; 2,001 source files still fail closed with AUTO_ACTIVATION_GIT_TOO_LARGE.
validation.diff_check: git diff --check passed for the changed files.

errors_and_intervention.initial_validation_error: The first test assertion called an unfiltered Python status helper and therefore hit the same intentional 2,000-source-entry guard.
errors_and_intervention.resolution: The test was corrected to compare the Node identity fingerprint with the canonical Python fingerprint helper; no product behavior was weakened.
errors_and_intervention.manual_intervention: One source-test assertion correction; no production intervention.

behavior_confirmation.outcome: workspaceIdentity accepted the current repository and returned a source fingerprint.

timing.timing_scope: observed reproduction-to-behavior interval plus separately measured focused validation; not total end-to-end agent wall time
